Design
Why

Model-driven loop on stop_reason
Claude chooses each call from the results
Several concerns in one message

A multi-concern request needs every part covered
Workload mixes both kinds
Route known paths to sequences, the rest to the loop
Each kind of work gets the design that fits it
Fixed tree shows no gain on any category
Keep the loop everywhere
Scripting brings no benefit
Many lookups just to learn what exists
MCP resource catalog
Fewer exploratory calls
Need to understand a code flow
Grep entry points, then Read along the calls
Incremental, not read-all
maps.rule: Use a fixed sequence where the path is known in advance. When each step depends on the last result, let the model choose the tool calls and loop until stop_reason is end_turn.

Branch on stop_reason

Let the model choose the next step from results

Case-facts block; trim tool results

Scratchpad file or subagent delegation
Picks the wrong tool
Weak tool descriptions
Expand tool descriptions
Loop ends too early, too late or never

Needless sequencing

Independent tasks run one after another
Multiple Task calls in one response
Parallel spawning

Structured error back to the coordinator, saying what was tried
The hub owns recovery
maps.rule: If a subagent's request depends on everyone's work or can change the plan, route it through the coordinator. Give a scoped cross-role tool only for frequent, simple, uniform needs.
